public_rationale: Research available before the post establishes recurring reconstruction. Nasr and colleagues reported extracting more than 10,000 distinct examples from ChatGPT under a targeted attack. Lee and colleagues separately measured verbatim training-text copying in more than 1% of unprompted output in their experiments. These findings support the ordinary reading that reconstruction can occur repeatedly. They do not establish a universal frequency, and the deduplication findings show that training practices matter.
limitations: Marcus supplies no numerical meaning for 'some regularity'.
Experimental output rates do not directly measure ordinary chatbot use.
The cited evidence supports recurrence, not universal susceptibility or any particular account of how model weights represent text.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Reconstruction of training text by large language models can happen with some regularity.

statement.excerpt: But the variety of the examples along with the technical literature on memorization and data leakage in large language models make clear that this kind of reconstruction certainly can happen with some regularity.

from_speaker: certainly can happen with some regularity
technical literature on memorization and data leakage
our_interpretation: Reconstruction means generating substantial verbatim passages from training text, beyond merely reproducing text supplied in the prompt.

The plain reading of 'can happen with some regularity' is a recurring, experimentally measurable phenomenon across examples. It does not specify a percentage of ordinary conversations or require every model to reproduce training text.

The claim concerns an established capability as of 2024-02-05 and expressly invokes earlier research. The target period therefore ends on the post date and has no stated beginning. This capability has no quarterly or annual reporting period.
criteria.support_condition: Pre-publication experiments demonstrate repeated verbatim reproduction of training passages across many examples, with counts or rates that establish recurrence rather than an isolated anecdote.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable experiments show that the purported repeated reconstructions were not training-text reproductions, or that reconstruction was confined to isolated, unrepeatable cases under the tested conditions.

evidence.explanation: Thousands of distinct extracted examples establish recurrence under a targeted attack. Because ChatGPT's training corpus was unavailable, the researchers checked matches against a large auxiliary corpus; this is less direct than verification against a disclosed training set.

The measured share of unprompted output demonstrates recurring training-text reproduction beyond targeted chatbot attacks. The percentage describes generated output in these experiments, not the percentage of ordinary conversations affected.

Deduplication reduces vulnerability, so extraction results cannot establish a uniform rate across models and training practices. This qualifies the scope of the supporting evidence without contradicting the claim that reconstruction can recur.
